source.title: Trap of Feature Diversity in the Learning of MLPs
source.authors: Dong-Rui Liu; Shaobo Wang; Jie Ren; Kangrui Wang; Sheng Yin; Huiqi Deng; Quan-Shi Zhang

record.file_problem: Complete paper text, including supplementary sections, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper measures training accuracy and loss during early training, addressing whether MLPs remain at high training error early on. It uses a different focus and measures feature diversity and learning phases rather than reproducing the claim’s benchmark memorization recipes.
record.gate_note: The paper reports training-accuracy results at the end of the first phase on CIFAR-10 and MNIST, and training-loss behavior during two-phase learning. Other results measure feature and gradient cosine similarity, weight-change components, or the duration of the first phase; they do not directly measure the training-error claim. No CIFAR-100 or corrupted-label result is reported.
record.test_reason: Appendix B directly compares training loss under two initialization variances in otherwise identical plain MLPs: increasing variance resolves stalled training. This bears on V4's initialization-dependent training speed. The extracted early-accuracy rows do not test V1.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors explain early feature-diversity decline through self-reinforcing common learning directions and explain how normalization, momentum, initialization, and L2 regularization can alleviate it. Their analysis establishes neither necessary nor sufficient conditions.
record.recipe_differences: Studies MLP learning dynamics and early training accuracy/feature diversity; it does not use the claim’s training-error endpoint as its primary measurement or test the cited memorization recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that first-phase duration or feature-diversity behavior changes with normalization, initialization variance, momentum, and L2 regularization; those comparisons measure feature similarity and phase duration, not training classification error.

fits_no_version.finding: At the end of the first phase, only one or two categories have training accuracy substantially above random guessing in CIFAR-10 and MNIST MLPs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Early MLP training can concentrate learning on a small subset of categories before broader learning begins.

fits_no_version.finding: Batch normalization reduces feature similarity, while initialization variance, momentum, and weight decay affect feature-diversity dynamics.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Common optimization choices can alleviate early feature-diversity collapse in MLPs.

record.code_released: not stated; the paper says code will be released when accepted.
record.problems: The relevant training-accuracy outcomes are presented in figures without numeric values in the supplied text. The reported accuracy findings are limited to the end of the first phase and do not resolve final training error after longer training.
record.rows_left_out: No additional training-accuracy rows were extracted from appendix figures because their plotted values are not readable in the supplied text and the text does not state distinct outcomes for those model configurations. Feature similarity and weight-change measurements do not directly measure a version’s named training-error behavior.

untested.parts: Near-zero training classification error in sufficiently large convolutional networks on CIFAR-10 or CIFAR-100, including corrupted labels, and the stated recipe-dependent exceptions.
Teacher-student spurious minima and the effect of adding one or two student neurons.
Depth-dependent training degradation in plain convolutional networks and its prevention by identity shortcuts or special initialization.
Activation matching, preservation of signal and gradient magnitudes, trainable-depth limits, orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization, and 10,000-layer convolutional networks.
Recovery above a measured stability threshold, curvature reduction, edge-of-stability dynamics, and divergence thresholds.
Accuracy gains over training time, tolerance of higher learning rates, and Fixup comparisons. The normalization experiments report feature similarity rather than these outcomes.

missing.what: The controlled initialization comparison: a nine-layer, 512-neuron-per-layer CIFAR-10 MLP stalls with variance multiplier 0.1, while an otherwise identical MLP with multiplier 1 escapes the stall. Record the qualitative training-loss outcome without inventing numeric endpoints.

record.verdict_notes: Remove the record's V1 limits_scope verdict: early MLP accuracy does not qualify the stated convolutional-network claim. The V4 support concerns training speed only; the proposed signal-propagation mechanism and greater trainable depth remain untested.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test CIFAR-100, corrupted or random labels, Adam, or whether sufficiently long training reaches near-zero error across the benchmark recipes in the version.

rows.subject: MLPs
rows.operation_detail: Measured training accuracy at the end of the first phase.
rows.measure: Training accuracy by category; the authors state that only one or two categories were learned above random guessing.
rows.value: figure only; text states that only a single or two categories had much higher accuracy than random guessing
rows.note: The result concerns the early first phase, not the final accuracy after training long enough. The figure does not provide readable numeric values in the supplied text.
rows.check: The qualitative result is correctly reported, but it concerns an MLP at an early training stage. It cannot establish V1's training-error outcome for sufficiently large convolutional networks.

rows.operation_detail: Measured training accuracy at the end of the first phase.

rows.value: figure only; text states that only a single or two categories had much higher accuracy than random guessing
rows.note: The result concerns the early first phase, not the final accuracy after training long enough. The figure does not provide readable numeric values in the supplied text.
rows.check: The qualitative result is correctly reported, but MNIST MLP accuracy at an early training stage does not measure V1's convolutional-network outcome on CIFAR-10 or CIFAR-100.

relationships.condition: Nine-layer plain ReLU MLPs with 512 neurons per layer on CIFAR-10; initialization variance multiplier increased from 0.1 to 1.
relationships.reason: Appendix B explicitly reports stalled loss minimization at 0.1 and resolution of the stall at 1 with initialization variance as the only change; this supports initialization-dependent training speed. Based on text and Figure 24, missing from the extracted rows.
relationships.display_finding: Increasing the initialization variance multiplier from 0.1 to 1 resolved stalled loss minimization with no other change.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: CIFAR-10 and MNIST MLPs at the end of the first phase
reader_labels.reason: The authors report that learning at this stage is concentrated in only one or two categories, so early training has not yet learned the full classification task (R1, R2). This does not establish the outcome after sufficiently long training.
